classification.habit: Small deciduous, milky-latex-bearing tree or shrub
classification.habitat: Tropical and subtropical forests, scrub and sub-Himalayan tracts
classification.distribution: Widely distributed in India, including tropical and sub-Himalayan regions

identification.description: Small deciduous tree with opposite leaves, fragrant white flowers and paired elongated follicles; latex is present in the plant.
identification.whole_plant: Small to medium deciduous tree or shrub, often with a spreading crown.
identification.root: Woody root system; not the principal official crude-drug part in this record.
identification.stem: Woody, branched stem with grey-brown bark and milky latex.
identification.leaf: Simple, opposite, elliptic to ovate-oblong leaves with prominent venation.
identification.flower: White, fragrant flowers arranged in terminal or axillary cymose clusters.
identification.fruit: Paired long, slender follicles containing numerous seeds.
identification.seed: Oblong seeds with a tuft of hairs at the apex; the seed is known as Indrayava.
identification.bark: Grey-brown bark; stem bark is an important medicinal part.

dosha.vata: May aggravate Vata when used excessively because of Laghu-Ruksha qualities

therapeutics.dose: Bark/seed powder: 3–6 g; decoction: 50–100 ml, with preparation-specific variation. Use an authoritative formulation reference for prescribing.
therapeutics.precautions: Authenticate the species and distinguish Kutaja bark from Indrayava seed. Persistent or severe diarrhoea requires appropriate clinical assessment.

shlokas:
कुटजः कूटजः कीटो वत्सको गिरिमल्लिका ।
कालिङ्गः शक्रशाखी च मल्लिकापुष्प इत्यपि ।
इन्द्रो यवफलः प्रोक्तो वृक्षकः पाण्डुरद्रुमः ॥१०१॥

कुटजः कटुको रूक्षो दीपनस्तुवरो हिमः ।
अर्शोऽतिसारपित्तास्रकफतृष्णामकुष्ठनुत् ॥१०२॥

phytochemistry.chemical_notes: Holarrhena bark and seeds contain characteristic steroidal alkaloids; exact composition varies by plant part and preparation.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Holarrhena pubescens is studied for its alkaloid-rich bark and seed drugs and for gastrointestinal indications. Modern evidence is preparation-specific and is not presented as proof of clinical efficacy.
modern_information.safety_notes: Use authenticated material and clinically appropriate dosing references; do not self-treat severe diarrhoea or dysentery.

exam_points: Useful parts: stem bark and Indrayava seed
Rasa: Tikta-Kashaya; Guna: Laghu-Ruksha; Virya: Sheeta; Vipaka: Katu
Kutaja is classically associated with Atisara and Grahani
viva_questions: What is the botanical name of Kutaja?
mnemonics: Kutaja = Kurchi bark + Indrayava seed + Grahi
student.quick_revision: Kutaja (Holarrhena pubescens): Apocynaceae tree; bark and Indrayava seed are important drugs; Tikta-Kashaya, Laghu-Ruksha, Sheeta, Katu profile.

teaching_points: Demonstrate the opposite leaves, white flowers and paired follicles.
Distinguish Kutaja bark from Indrayava seed as separate crude-drug parts.
practical_points: Examine bark, leaf and follicle morphology.
Identify the hairy-tipped seeds when available.

doctor.quick_reference: Kutaja is a classical Grahi drug used chiefly in Atisara/Grahani contexts; bark and Indrayava should be treated as distinct crude-drug parts.
doctor.dose: 3–6 g powder or 50–100 ml decoction are reported in the referenced educational source; verify formulation-specific dosing.
key_precautions: Seek clinical evaluation for severe or persistent diarrhoea
